title: Indirect object pronouns: lui, leur
goal: By the end of this lesson you can replace 'à + person' with lui or leur, recognise the verbs that need them, and tell direct from indirect objects.

body: An indirect object is a person linked to the verb by *à*: *Je parle* **à Marie**. *J'écris* **à mes parents**. *Je donne un cadeau* **à mon frère**.
To replace it, use *lui* (to him or to her) or *leur* (to them). *Lui* is used for both men and women: *Je* **lui** *parle* can mean 'I talk to him' or 'I talk to her'.

head: Person
Pronoun
Example
rows: Il me téléphone. Il te téléphone.

learn.tip: Lui = him OR her. Leur = them. Never add -s to the pronoun leur.

body: Learn these verbs with their *à*. Many are verbs of communication and giving: you speak *to* someone, give something *to* someone.

Watch out: some verbs that take a direct object in English take *à* in French (*téléphoner à*, *répondre à*, *ressembler à*), and some do the opposite (*attendre*, *écouter*, *regarder*, *chercher* take a direct object).

learn.h: Placement: same rules as le, la, les
body: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: *Je* **lui** *parle*. Negative: *Je ne* **lui** *parle pas*.
With an infinitive it goes before the infinitive: *Je vais* **leur** *écrire*. In the passé composé it goes before *avoir*: *Je* **lui** *ai dit la vérité*.
Important difference: there is **no** agreement of the past participle with an indirect object. *Je leur ai parlé* (no -s).

learn.h: Direct or indirect? The à test
body: Ask: is there an *à* before the person? *J'aide Marie* (no à) → *Je l'aide*. *Je parle à Marie* (à) → *Je lui parle*.
*Lui* and *leur* are for people (and animals). For things after *à*, French uses *y*, which we will see in lesson 47: *Je pense à mon voyage* → *J'y pense*.
In a positive command, the pronoun follows the verb: *Parle-***lui**! *Répondez-***leur**! *Donne-***moi** *ça!* (me becomes *moi* at the end).
In a negative command, it goes back in front: *Ne* **lui** *dis pas!* *Ne* **leur** *réponds pas!*

examples.fr: Tu parles à ta mère? Oui, je lui parle tous les jours.
examples.en: Do you talk to your mother? Yes, I talk to her every day.

examples.fr: Je lui ai donné mon numéro.
examples.en: I gave him / her my number.

examples.fr: Mes grands-parents? Je leur écris une carte.
examples.en: My grandparents? I'm writing them a card.
I'm going to call them tomorrow.
You look a lot like him / her.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu lui as dit?
examples.en: What did you tell him / her?

examples.fr: Je leur ai demandé de venir à six heures.
examples.en: I asked them to come at six.
examples.note: demander à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose

examples.fr: Envoie-moi un texto quand tu arrives.
examples.en: Send me a text when you get there.

examples.fr: Ne lui dis pas mon secret!
examples.en: Don't tell him / her my secret!
examples.note: negative command: pronoun before the verb

examples.fr: Le prof nous explique la règle.
examples.en: The teacher explains the rule to us.

examples.fr: Je vous souhaite une bonne journée.
examples.en: I wish you a good day.

examples.fr: Ce film ne leur plaît pas.
examples.note: plaire à: literally 'this movie doesn't please them'

examples.fr: Mes voisins? Je les aide et je leur parle souvent.
examples.en: My neighbours? I help them and I often talk to them.
examples.note: aider (direct: les) vs parler à (indirect: leur)

examples.fr: On lui a offert un chandail pour sa fête.
examples.en: We gave him / her a sweater for his / her birthday.
examples.note: offrir à; chandail = sweater in Quebec

examples.fr: Ça te dit d'aller au cinéma?
examples.en: Do you feel like going to the movies?

quebec.intro: In casual Quebec speech, 'lui' is very often replaced by 'y' (pronounced [i]): 'je lui ai dit' becomes 'j'y ai dit'. You will hear it constantly; in writing and formal speech always use lui. Leur usually stays leur.

items.en: I'm going to talk to him / her.

items.std: Je ne lui ai pas répondu.
items.note: ne dropped, y for lui; informal
leur is kept; only je shortens

drills.why: À + several people = leur, which never takes -s.

drills.q: Which verb takes a DIRECT object in French?

drills.why: Parler à = indirect; Julie is one person: lui.

drills.q: Mes parents? Je ___ téléphone le dimanche. (them)
drills.en: My parents? I call them on Sundays.

drills.q: Ta sœur? Je ___ ai envoyé un message. (to her)
drills.en: Your sister? I sent her a message.
drills.why: Envoyer à quelqu'un: lui for her.
Me before the verb in the negative.

drills.en: I'm going to talk to her.

drills.a: Nous lui avons donné un cadeau.

drills.why: Ressembler à takes an indirect object.

pron.tip: One syllable [lwi], glide quickly from u to i. Not 'loo-ee'.
[lœr], like 'lur' with rounded lips; leur and leurs sound the same.
In speech often 'leur dis pas!' with ne dropped.

dialogue.fr: C'est la fête de grand-maman dimanche. Qu'est-ce qu'on lui offre?
dialogue.en: It's Grandma's birthday on Sunday. What are we giving her?

dialogue.fr: On peut lui offrir un beau foulard.
dialogue.en: We can give her a nice scarf.

dialogue.fr: Bonne idée. As-tu parlé à tes cousins?
dialogue.en: Good idea. Have you talked to your cousins?

dialogue.fr: Oui, je leur ai envoyé un texto hier, mais ils ne m'ont pas répondu.
dialogue.en: Yes, I sent them a text yesterday, but they haven't answered me.

dialogue.fr: Téléphone-leur ce soir. Pis matante Lise?
dialogue.en: Call them tonight. And Aunt Lise?

dialogue.fr: J'y ai dit de venir à cinq heures.
dialogue.en: I told her to come at five.

dialogue.fr: Parfait. Mais surtout, ne dis rien à grand-maman!
dialogue.en: Perfect. But above all, don't say anything to Grandma!

dialogue.fr: Promis, je ne lui dis rien.
dialogue.en: Promise, I won't tell her anything.

questions.q: What gift do they plan to give?
Why should A's sibling call the cousins?
What time is Aunt Lise coming?

speak.prompt: Answer with lui or leur: 'Tu parles souvent à ta mère? Tu écris à tes amis? Tu as répondu à ton patron?'
speak.model: Oui, je lui parle souvent. Non, je ne leur écris pas, je leur envoie des textos. Oui, je lui ai répondu ce matin.

speak.prompt: Give three commands to a friend about someone else: tell him, call them, don't answer her.
speak.model: Dis-lui bonjour! Téléphone-leur ce soir! Ne lui réponds pas!

speak.prompt: Say 'I told him to wait' in standard French, then in casual Quebec style.
speak.model: Je lui ai dit d'attendre. / J'y ai dit d'attendre.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about how you stay in touch with family and friends. Use lui and leur at least four times.
write.model: Ma mère habite à Sherbrooke. Je lui téléphone tous les dimanches. Mes frères habitent en Ontario, alors je leur envoie souvent des textos. Pour la fête de mon père, je lui ai offert un livre. Mes amis me manquent, mais je leur parle sur Internet. Je vais leur rendre visite cet été.

quiz.why: Lui is used for both masculine and feminine indirect objects.
Aider takes a direct object: je l'aide.
No agreement with an indirect object.
At the end of a positive command, me becomes moi.
Plaire à: literally 'does it please you?'

quiz.q: In Quebec speech, 'J'y ai dit' usually means…
Which verb needs 'à' before a person in French?

quiz.why: Écrire à + plural: leur, before the infinitive.
